deep.reconstruction:
Folio 77 (old number 103 struck), Litt. K, headed 'Berechnung der elliptischen Elemente. Als Beispiel die [planet symbol] 1806 nach diesen Elementen' (calculation of the elliptic elements; as an example, the planet marked with a sickle-like symbol, 1806, computed from these elements). The preceding page has a node and inclination determination with i = 10 deg 37' 30.5" and node about 80 deg 56' 22.6", which fits Ceres (a about 2.77, e about 0.08, node about 80.9 deg). So this is most likely Ceres, but the identification rests on the numbers and is not certain. The page is a worked numerical test: from a set of orbital elements, compute an ephemeris position for the date 1806 March 17, 4h 312777 (= day 76.17969907 of the year count used), and compare with an observation. It is the forward (ephemeris) direction of the method of Theoria Motus.

1. Left column (top): numbers 0,4157328 / 0,4071810 / 0,0085518 / 0,0021379 1/2 and 0 deg 8' 27" 29.5/42, 0.16.55 17/42 (53), 7.14.37 8/87 are interpolation work: differences of logarithms carried over from the previous page (the r values 0,4157595, 0,4106122, 0,4072165), with fractional parts of an interpolation interval. Their exact role is unclear. Then a chain of logarithms (7.6922176, 9.1006765, 5.3844352, 8.2013530, ...) leads to 8.2160480, then 0,8333333.33 (log of 1/... = a constant, 0.8333 = 5/6) and 164455.34, then 0,8497789, +111, 0,4114569 (log r, heliocentric distance, r about 2.58) and 9.7130035, 0.6984534. These are the usual log-table steps for the radius vector and the quantity (1+e cos)/... The details of each multiplication are not fully legible to me.

2. Central struck-out block (two big X's): an earlier attempt at the same reduction with the numbers 4.2176468 (= log of e in seconds, e*206265"), 8.9032217 (= log e, e = 0.08002), 9.66..., 1111208, 0,4419747 (= log a, a = 2.7668), 0,4099380, 74564, then angle sums 8.52.50,33 + 16.18.53,22 = 25.11.43,55, +2.6.19.80 = 27.17.53,65, etc., ending 176.7.51.05. This block is crossed out; I read it as an abandoned or superseded computation, replaced by the clean block immediately to the right.

3. Right block (kept): columns of logarithms with angle sums 9 deg 4' 30.33" + 16.18.53,22 = 25.23.23,55; +2.7.3,64 = 27.30.27,19; +2.11.56,36 = 29.42.23,55; + 65.37.4.49 = 95.19.28,04 ... + 80 56 33,06 = 176.21.33,51; heliocentric longitude 17 deg 7' 57".39 (mod 360 shown as 17.7.57,39). Written: 'Error long. hel. +4".0, latit. geoc: -5".5', i.e. the computed ephemeris differs from the observation by +4".0 in heliocentric longitude and -5".5 in geocentric latitude. Interpretation (mine): the sums are mean anomaly at epoch + motion + equation of centre (angle for the true anomaly) + perihelion argument + node, giving longitude, with the log columns giving sin/cos factors for reduction to the ecliptic and latitude.

4. Middle block, Kepler's equation. '8,9032217 e' with 'Med. ex. 29 deg 21' 23".085' (the eccentric anomaly E = 29 deg 21' 23.085"). Two columns of logs multiply e (in seconds, 4.2176468, and 2e, 4.5186768, since 4.5186768 - 4.2176468 = 0.30103 = log 2) by trigonometric factors, giving 3.8958348 and 3.8280913 (log seconds). The result 27.30.29,68 / 1 52.11 18 / 25.38.18"50 'Motus' appears to be a step of an iterative solution of E - e sin E = M for the mean anomaly. Below this, tg(phi/2) and sin lines: 9.4122599 tg 1/2 phi, 9.0680737 1/2 sin, 8.4803336, 8.4817287 and 9.3982264 'sin', 0,4114569 (log r), 9067850, 4.9487967, 4.0704599, 0.4419747, 0.6629620 1/2, 'Bon', 7867465: these produce the true anomaly from the eccentric anomaly (tan(v/2) = sqrt((1+e)/(1-e)) tan(E/2)), and the distance r = a(1 - e cos E). Note: e = sin phi with phi = 4 deg 35' 29".86 (written '= phi'), which is the standard Gaussian angle of eccentricity (Theoria Motus uses phi with e = sin phi).

5. Left lower block: 'half epsilon 6 deg 45' 52".4195'; 7.14.37.9925; 14.0.29.6156; 0.28.44.6734; further logs 7.6922176, 9.9999848, 9.9868886 ... 9.3843627 'Gut' leading to 2 deg 17' 40".29 and 4.35.29.86 = phi. This is the determination of phi (hence e) and the mean-anomaly pieces from the preceding elements; 'Gut' means 'good' (check agrees).

6. Lower right, final elements: 'Anom. verae' 46.6.16.350 (value unclear), 68 16 39 15, 114.22.55.50; 65.37.4.47 and 65.37.4.50 (argument of perihelion, two slightly different values compared); node 80.56.22.685; 'Perihel. 146.33.27.10' = node + argument of perihelion (146 33 27.15 when added; the page gives .10, which fits the lower value used); 'Motus d. in. 770".9825' (daily mean motion, 770.9825 arcsec per day); 29 deg 21' 23".085 minus 2 11 7.465 = 27 10 15.62 'Epocha anom. m.' (epoch mean anomaly); 'Motus 65845.29' ; 9.4.30,33 'Epocha 1805'; 146.33.27,10 + 9.4.30,33 = 155.37.57,43 'Epocha der Laenge' (epoch of the longitude, mean longitude at the epoch). Far right: 14.38.10.47 (-0".12) and 14.20.17.90 (-0".05), comparison numbers for the previous page's third-hypothesis result (14.38.10,59 and 14.20.17,95), apparently residuals of 0.12 and 0.05 arcsec, i.e. the new elements reproduce the earlier hypothesis values to about a tenth of an arcsecond.

Problem served: converting the fitted orbit (from the three 'Hypotheses' tested on the previous page) into the standard set of elliptic elements: epoch, mean motion, longitude of perihelion, node, inclination, e and a, and verifying them by recomputing one observed place (1806 March 17) with a residual of a few arcseconds. This is a routine numerical consistency check in the workflow of the Theoria motus corporum coelestium (1809), written in logarithms to seven places.
errors: Possible slip or an unresolved arithmetic step: e sin E using e = 0.080024 (log 8.9032217) and E = 29 deg 21' 23.085" gives e sin E = 8092" = 2 deg 14' 52", so M = E - e sin E should be 27 deg 6' 31". The page subtracts 2 deg 11' 7.465" (7867.465") and gets 27 deg 10' 15.62" Epocha anom. m. The 7867.465 corresponds to a sine factor log 9.678188 (sin about 0.4767), not log sin E = 9.6904. This may mean the quantity subtracted is not simply e sin E at this E (for instance a correction in an iteration, or E being a different intermediate), or a misreading of mine. I cannot resolve it from the page; flagged as a discrepancy to check, not a confirmed error.

Mean daily motion 770.9825 arcsec versus 770.9765 from k/a^(3/2) with Gauss's k = 3548.18761" and log a = 0.4419747 (a = 2.76678). The difference is about 8e-6 in relative terms, which is plausible if the planet mass term or a more precise a was used, but is not reproduced from the numbers visible here.
Two values 65.37.4.47 and 65.37.4.50 are written for the argument of perihelion; they differ by 0.03", harmless but unreconciled.

Summation 80.56.22.685 + 65.37.4.47 = 146.33.27.155 while the page gives 146.33.27.10; this matches only with 22.62 + 4.48, so the node value used is nearer 80.56.22.62 (previous page gives 80.56.22.60 / 80 56 22.615). Minor rounding level.
The identification of the planet as Ceres is inferred from the elements; the page itself shows only a symbol.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine numerical working page in the Ceres/Theoria Motus workflow: elements to ephemeris, with logarithmic multiplications and a residual check. It contains no new method or result beyond what Gauss published in 1809, and the one anomaly (the e sin E value) looks like an intermediate step or a reading problem, not a mathematical novelty.
